MSRC_YEAR_MONTH.description: Mandatory Patch Tuesday release slug. Accepts the canonical YYYY-MMM form (e.g. '2026-May', '2026-Jan' — full month name or 3-letter abbreviation, case-insensitive) and the YYYY-MM numeric form (e.g. '2026-05'); the numeric form is translated to the title-case month name MSRC's URL path expects before the request is issued. Malformed input aborts the run with an explicit error so the operator can correct the manifest. Microsoft publishes one CVRF document per release on Patch Tuesday (second Tuesday of every month); the slug uniquely identifies that release in the MSRC update guide.

MSRC_PRODUCT.description: Optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the affected-product set after the CVRF document is fetched. A CVE is kept when any of its affected ProductID -> FullProductName mappings contain the filter substring; otherwise it is dropped. Blank / missing input keeps every CVE in the release (the typical operational mode where the operator wants the whole Patch Tuesday rollup). Vulns with no resolvable products are DROPPED when a filter is set (we cannot prove they match the filter) but KEPT when no filter is supplied.

name: msrc
title: Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) CVRF
description: Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) CVRF feed importer. Pulls the monthly Microsoft Security Update Guide release as a CVRF (Common Vulnerability Reporting Framework) document from the public MSRC REST API (https://api.msrc.microsoft.com/cvrf/v3.0/cvrf/{YYYY-MMM}) and emits Faraday bulk-create JSON. Microsoft publishes one CVRF document per Patch Tuesday release; each document carries every CVE Microsoft addressed that month with per-product affected-version metadata, CVSS scoring, exploit status, and the canonical KB / advisory remediation URLs. Endpoint used: GET https://api.msrc.microsoft.com/cvrf/v3.0/cvrf/{YYYY-MMM} (returns the canonical envelope {DocumentTitle, DocumentTracking, DocumentPublisher, ProductTree, Vulnerability: [...]}). MSRC_YEAR_MONTH is mandatory and accepts either YYYY-MMM (full month name or 3-letter abbreviation, case-insensitive) or YYYY-MM numeric form; both are normalised to the title-case slug MSRC's URL path expects. MSRC_PRODUCT is an optional case-insensitive substring filter applied to the affected-product set after the document is fetched; blank input keeps every CVE in the release. Each CVE becomes one Faraday vulnerability under a single synthetic 0.0.0.0 host with hostname 'msrc' (MSRC entries are CVE-keyed not host-keyed — the operator's other agents emit the host-side findings this feed is correlated against). The vulnerability carries tags: ['msrc'] and surfaces the CVE id, MSRC title, affected products, CVSS score / severity / vector, exploit status, and KB / advisory remediation URLs in both the description and the refs list. Severity is derived from CVSS — the explicit BaseSeverity text (Critical / Important / Moderate / Low / None) is mapped to Faraday's ladder (Important -> high per MSRC's published severity rubric) when present, falling back to a numeric BaseScore bucket (>=9.0 critical / >=7.0 high / >=4.0 medium / >0.0 low / 0.0 info). Unscored CVEs default to 'info' — we don't synthesise a ranking MSRC hasn't published. CVEs whose Threats block flags 'Exploited: Yes' / 'Exploit Code Maturity: Functional' are bumped to 'critical' regardless of the CVSS bucket — active exploitation overrides the calendar floor. Refs include the canonical NVD CVE permalink (https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-...), the MSRC update guide vulnerability permalink (https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-...), every Remediation URL with its Type tag as a suffix, and explicit Msrc-CveID / Msrc-CvssVersion / Msrc-CvssScore / Msrc-CvssSeverity / Msrc-CvssVector / Msrc-Exploited / Msrc-Threats / Msrc-AffectedProductCount / Msrc-ReleaseID / Msrc-CurrentReleaseDate / Msrc-InitialReleaseDate pivots. Status is always open (an MSRC entry cannot be 'fixed' in the catalog — it can only be remediated on the affected hosts). Auth: MSRC_API_KEY is an optional 'api-key' HTTP header on every request — the MSRC developer portal at https://msrc.microsoft.com/developer issues free keys after signup but the API also tolerates unauthenticated requests at a lower rate ceiling. MSRC_HOST may optionally be overridden via env to point at a federated mirror or an offline cache; defaults to https://api.msrc.microsoft.com. Tags: [msrc].
